 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Chicago Bears just lost their most reliable player for the rest of the 2026 season. Cole Kmet suffered a serious knee injury on Thursday night and will miss the final games. Coach Ben Johnson confirmed the news on Friday. The team placed Kmet on injured reserve immediately. This hit hurts deep because Kmet is the longest-tenured player on the roster. He is a true Chicago native who grew up loving the team. Losing him changes everything for the offense right now.
 A Giant Hole in the Lineup
 Kmet was a key piece in the win over New England. He caught an 8-yard pass before colliding with two defenders. The injury happened late in the fourth quarter. He could not put weight on his leg and had to be carted off. According to ESPN , he recorded 10 catches, 87 yards, and a touchdown across seven games. Those numbers look small, but his role was much bigger. He played 62.2% of offensive snaps this season. His blocking helped the rushing attack stay strong all year. "He's everything we want to be about here," Johnson said. "He's going to be sorely missed. Really, he's Chicago." That quote from Johnson shows how vital he was to the culture.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Rookies Must Step Up Fast
 The team has no time to grieve. Someone else has to step up right away. In seven games, rookie Sam Roush has managed only three receptions totaling 33 yards. The coaching staff is pleased with his improvement so far. "We've been very pleased with the improvement that he's made over these first seven weeks," Johnson said. But Roush is not ready to replace Kmet's full workload yet. Colston Loveland has started to heat up with 134 yards in his last two games. He is the only one with real momentum. Stephen Carlson and Qadir Ismail are also on the Bears practice squad. Hayden Large could be activated from injured reserve too. Yet none of them are Kmet. "It stinks, it does. I hate it for him," Johnson said. "And yet the train keeps rolling along."
 The Financial Reality Looms
 This injury also brings a tough financial question for the front office. Following the team's restructuring of his deal back in April, Kmet's cap hit increased. According to Sports Illustrated , the Bears can cut him for a dead-money charge of $5.4 million. They would save $10 million if they release him. That is a lot of money to lose on a player who cannot play. The team needs to decide his future soon. Kmet has 22 touchdowns during his career with the Bears. He joined Hall of Famer Mike Ditka on a list of special Bears players. His absence leaves a gap that money cannot fix. The Bears must find a way to win without their glue guy.
